title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 3 — Angles
question: How do you name angles and find missing angles on a line, around a point, in a triangle and on parallel lines?
intro:
Chapter 3 is about naming and finding angles. A few facts do most of the work, drawn in the figure: angles on a straight line add up to \(180^\circ\), angles around a point add up to \(360^\circ\), vertically opposite angles are equal, the angles of a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\), and parallel lines make pairs of angles that are equal or add up to \(180^\circ\). Labels 3.1 to 3.5 name the parts of this page. Every card has several examples of the same kind — try each one, then tap **Show working**.

**By the end of the chapter:** name an angle by its size, and find a missing angle on a straight line, around a point, in a triangle and on parallel lines.
figure_alt: Six angle facts: angles on a straight line add to 180°, around a point to 360°, vertically opposite angles are equal, a triangle's angles add to 180°, an exterior angle equals the two opposite inside angles, and parallel lines give equal F and Z angles and C angles that add to 180°.

questions.title: Name the angle
questions.prompt:
An angle is named by its size:

\[\begin{aligned} \text{acute} &: \text{less than } 90^\circ \\ \text{right} &: \text{exactly } 90^\circ \\ \text{obtuse} &: \text{between } 90^\circ \text{ and } 180^\circ \\ \text{straight} &: \text{exactly } 180^\circ \\ \text{reflex} &: \text{between } 180^\circ \text{ and } 360^\circ \end{aligned}\]

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(35^\circ\)
- **b)** \(90^\circ\)
- **c)** \(128^\circ\)
- **d)** \(210^\circ\)

questions.title: Close to the borders
questions.prompt:
Check the border numbers carefully: \(89^\circ\) is still acute, but \(91^\circ\) is already obtuse.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(89^\circ\)
- **b)** \(91^\circ\)
- **c)** \(180^\circ\)
- **d)** \(345^\circ\)
steps:
**c)** Half a turn — a straight line:

\[180^\circ \to \boxed{\text{straight angle}}\]

questions.title: Two angles on a straight line
questions.prompt:
Angles on a straight line **add up to \(180^\circ\)**. The missing angle is \(180^\circ\) minus the angle you know.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(x\) and \(130^\circ\)
- **b)** \(x\) and \(72^\circ\)
- **c)** \(x\) and \(90^\circ\)
- **d)** \(x\) and \(155^\circ\)

questions.title: Three angles on a straight line
questions.prompt:
Add the angles you know, then take the total from \(180^\circ\).

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(40^\circ\), \(65^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **b)** \(90^\circ\), \(35^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **c)** \(25^\circ\), \(25^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **d)** \(x\), \(x\) and \(100^\circ\) (two equal angles)

questions.group: 3.3 Angles at a Point and Vertically Opposite Angles
questions.title: Angles around a point
questions.prompt:
Angles all the way **around a point add up to \(360^\circ\)** — one full turn.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(150^\circ\), \(120^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **b)** \(200^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **c)** \(90^\circ\), \(90^\circ\), \(110^\circ\) and \(x\)
- **d)** \(100^\circ\), \(85^\circ\), \(95^\circ\) and \(x\)

questions.group: 3.3 Angles at a Point and Vertically Opposite Angles
questions.title: Vertically opposite angles
questions.prompt:
When two straight lines cross they make four angles. **Opposite angles are equal**, and **neighbouring angles add up to \(180^\circ\)** because they sit on a straight line.

**Examples:**

- **a)** One of the four angles is \(40^\circ\). Find the other three.
- **b)** One of the four angles is \(115^\circ\). Find the other three.
- **c)** One of the four angles is \(90^\circ\). Find the other three.
- **d)** One of the four angles is \(72^\circ\). Find the other three.
steps:
**c)** Opposite: \(90^\circ\). Neighbours: \(180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\) — all four are right angles.

\[\boxed{90^\circ,\ 90^\circ,\ 90^\circ}\]

questions.title: Angles in a triangle
questions.prompt:
The three angles of any triangle **add up to \(180^\circ\)**. Two angles are given; find the third.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(50^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\)
- **b)** \(90^\circ\) and \(35^\circ\)
- **c)** \(110^\circ\) and \(25^\circ\)
- **d)** \(60^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\)
steps:
**d)** \(60^\circ + 60^\circ = 120^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 120^\circ = \boxed{60^\circ}\]

All three angles are \(60^\circ\): an equilateral triangle.

questions.title: Isosceles triangles
questions.prompt:
An **isosceles** triangle has two equal sides, and the two **base angles** next to the third side are **equal**.

**Examples:**

- **a)** The top angle is \(40^\circ\). Find each base angle.
- **b)** Each base angle is \(65^\circ\). Find the top angle.
- **c)** The top angle is \(100^\circ\). Find each base angle.
- **d)** Each base angle is \(45^\circ\). Find the top angle.
steps:
**d)** The two base angles make \(90^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 90^\circ = \boxed{90^\circ}\]

A right angle at the top: a right-angled isosceles triangle.

questions.title: Exterior angle
questions.prompt:
Extend one side of a triangle. The **exterior angle** outside the triangle equals the **sum of the two opposite inside angles**. The two opposite inside angles are given; find the exterior angle.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(50^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\)
- **b)** \(35^\circ\) and \(80^\circ\)
- **c)** \(90^\circ\) and \(42^\circ\)
- **d)** \(28^\circ\) and \(47^\circ\)
steps:
**a)**

\[50^\circ + 60^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}\]

Check: the third inside angle is \(180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ\), and \(70^\circ + 110^\circ = 180^\circ\) on the straight line.

questions.title: Corresponding and alternate angles
questions.prompt:
A line crossing two **parallel** lines makes matching angles (see the figure). **Corresponding** angles, in an **F** shape, are **equal**. **Alternate** angles, in a **Z** shape, are **equal**.

**Examples:**

- **a)** Find the angle corresponding to \(70^\circ\).
- **b)** Find the angle alternate to \(125^\circ\).
- **c)** Find the angle corresponding to \(48^\circ\).
- **d)** Find the angle alternate to \(90^\circ\).
steps:
**d)** Alternate angles are equal:

\[\boxed{90^\circ}\]

The crossing line is at right angles to both lines.

questions.title: Co-interior angles
questions.prompt:
**Co-interior** angles, in a **C** shape, sit between the parallel lines on the same side. They **add up to \(180^\circ\)**.

**Examples:**

- **a)** One co-interior angle is \(110^\circ\). Find the other.
- **b)** One co-interior angle is \(75^\circ\). Find the other.
- **c)** One co-interior angle is \(90^\circ\). Find the other.
- **d)** One co-interior angle is \(136^\circ\). Find the other.
